bit.d: The smallest unit of information: 0 or 1. With n bits you can form exactly 2n different patterns; what each pattern means depends on the type it is read with.

byte.d: A group of 8 bits, the smallest unit memory can address. Tensor sizes, KV pools and memory bandwidths are counted in bytes.

hexadecimal.d: Base 16 (digits 0–9 and A–F). Each digit corresponds to exactly 4 bits, which is why it's the usual notation for bit patterns: 0xCBAC1FED is 32 bits.

dtype.d: The data type of a tensor (e.g., torch.bfloat16, uint8, float8_e4m3fn): it says how many bytes each element has and which rule turns those bytes into a number.

conteiner-de-armazenamento.d: The type used to store and move bytes, which may differ from the logical numeric format: two FP4 values inside a uint8, the EXL3 trellis in int16 words, DeepSeek's KV row as 584 uint8 bytes.

reinterpretacao-de-bytes.d: Reading the same bytes with another dtype, without copying or converting (tensor.view(dtype)). Unlike .to()/copy_(), which compute new bytes for the same value. Mixing the two up silently destroys data (e.g., an E8M0 scale of 2−7 converted to uint8 becomes 0).

inteiro-sem-sinal.d: Reading n bits as \( \sum_i b_i 2^i \), from 0 to 2n−1 (uint8: 0–255; uint32: up to 4,294,967,295).

complemento-de-dois.d: The standard representation of signed integers: the top bit weighs −2<sup>n−1</sup>. Range from −2<sup>n−1</sup> to 2<sup>n−1</sup>−1 (INT8: −128…127; INT4: −8…7). A single zero, the same adder works for signed and unsigned integers, and \(-x = \lnot x + 1\).

aritmetica-modular.d: n-bit hardware keeps only the low n bits of each result: addition and multiplication are done modulo 2n. It's a bug in counters and a feature in hashes and generators, like the MCG codebook (x·0xCBAC1FED mod 2³²).

overflow-de-inteiro.d: When the exact result doesn't fit in n bits and “wraps around”: 127 + 1 = −128 in INT8, and a pointer offset above 231−1 turns negative in int32. In C/C++ signed overflow is formally undefined; in hardware, the value simply wraps around.

aritmetica-de-ponteiros.d: Computing addresses such as base + index × stride inside kernels. If the product is done in int32, it overflows above 231−1 (≈ 2 GiB in bytes). That's why large caches promote the index to int64 before multiplying.

ponto-flutuante.d: Scientific notation in binary: \( x = (-1)^S\cdot 2^{E-\text{bias}}\cdot(1+M/2^m) \). Sign, exponent (range) and mantissa (precision) share the bits; the rounding error is relative to the size of the number.

expoente-com-bias.d: The exponent field is stored as an unsigned integer with an offset added (bias = 2<sup>e−1</sup>−1: 127 in FP32/BF16, 15 in FP16, 7 in E4M3). This keeps positive floats in the same order as their bit patterns read as integers.

mantissa.d: The bits that store the digits after the point in 1.f × 2<sup>e</sup>. Each extra bit halves the relative error: 23 bits in FP32, 10 in FP16, 7 in BF16, 3 in E4M3.

bit-implicito.d: Since every normal number in binary starts with “1.”, that 1 isn't stored, which gives one bit of precision for free. In subnormals (exponent 0) the implicit bit is 0.

subnormal.d: A number whose exponent field is 0: no implicit bit, with uniform steps between zero and the smallest normal (gradual underflow). E.g., 10<sup>−5</sup> is subnormal in FP16; 0.5 is the only positive subnormal of E2M1.

inf-nan.d: Special values of the IEEE formats, with the exponent all ones: mantissa 0 = ±∞ (overflow), mantissa ≠ 0 = NaN (“not a number”, e.g., ∞ − ∞). NaN contaminates every calculation it enters. The “fn” FP8 E4M3 has no ∞ and a single NaN per sign.

binade.d: The interval [2<sup>e</sup>, 2<sup>e+1</sup>). Every binade of a format has the same number of values (2<sup>m</sup>), so the absolute step doubles from one binade to the next and the relative step stays constant.

ulp.d: The distance between a float and the next one: 2<sup>e−m</sup> for x in [2<sup>e</sup>, 2<sup>e+1</sup>). In BF16, the ulp at 256 is 2; in FP32, the ulp at 10<sup>8</sup> is 8. Adding 1 to the bit pattern moves exactly one ulp.

fp32.d: 32-bit floating point: 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits (bias 127) and 23 mantissa bits. About 7 decimal digits and a range from ~10<sup>−38</sup> to 3.4·10<sup>38</sup>. It's the standard format for accumulators, routers, recurrent states and scales.

fp16.d: 16-bit IEEE floating point: 1 / 5 / 10 (bias 15). More precise than BF16 (ε = 2<sup>−10</sup>), but with a small range: maximum 65,504 and subnormals below 6.1·10<sup>−5</sup>. It appears where the range is guaranteed, such as inside GLM's EXL3 kernels and in the V of Qwen's PV dot.

bf16.d: Brain floating point: the top half of an FP32 (1 / 8 / 7, bias 127). It has the same range as FP32 with only ~2.4 decimal digits. It's the base format for serving: activations, non-quantized weights, lm_head and the “auto” KV.

epsilon-da-maquina.d: ε = 2<sup>−m</sup>, the distance from 1 to the next float (FP32 ≈ 1.19·10<sup>−7</sup>, FP16 ≈ 9.8·10<sup>−4</sup>, BF16 ≈ 7.8·10<sup>−3</sup>). The relative error of one rounding is at most u = ε/2.

arredondamento-rne.d: Round-to-nearest, ties-to-even, the default IEEE 754 mode: it picks the nearest representable neighbor and, on an exact tie, the one that ends in a 0 bit. Unlike truncation, it has no average bias.

overflow-float.d: A result above the largest finite value: in the IEEE formats it becomes ±∞ (FP16 starting at 65,520). In quantization, you saturate first with an explicit clamp, because formats like the fn E4M3 have no ∞.

saturacao-numerica.d: Clipping values into the range before converting, for example clamp(−448, 448) before .to(float8_e4m3fn). It trades a large but rare error (clipping) for never producing ∞ or NaN.

underflow.d: A result smaller than the smallest normal: first the subnormals lose bits gradually, and below the smallest subnormal the value becomes 0. With flush-to-zero, everything below the smallest normal becomes 0 at once.

flush-to-zero.d: A hardware/compiler mode that replaces subnormals with zero, because they're slow on some hardware. It's turned on, among other effects, by --use_fast_math.

fast-math.d: An nvcc flag that turns on approximations: flush-to-zero, approximate division and square root, and fast intrinsics (__expf). It changes the last bits of results; GLM's E3 kernel is compiled without it to reproduce torch.sigmoid.

absorcao.d: When |b| is smaller than half an ulp of a, a + b = a: the small term vanishes. E.g., 256 + 1 = 256 in BF16. That's why accumulating long sums in BF16 “stalls”.

cancelamento-catastrofico.d: Subtracting nearly equal numbers cancels the leading digits and leaves the operands' rounding errors front and center: the result has a large relative error.

acumulador.d: The variable in which a kernel adds up the partial products of a dot product or a GEMM. It can have more precision than the inputs: tensor cores take BF16/FP8/FP4 and accumulate in FP32.

fma.d: An instruction that computes a·b + c with a single rounding at the end. It's the atom of GEMMs, on both CUDA cores and tensor cores.

nao-associatividade.d: In floats, (a + b) + c ≠ a + (b + c) in general, because every addition rounds. E.g., in FP32: (10<sup>8</sup> + 1) − 10<sup>8</sup> = 0, but (10<sup>8</sup> − 10<sup>8</sup>) + 1 = 1. Changing the order of a reduction changes the bits of the result.

reducao-paralela.d: A sum (or max) of many values computed as a tree by many threads and blocks. The shape of the tree depends on the tiling, the batch size and on split-K or atomics. Since float addition isn't associative, the last bits change along with the shape.

bits-significativos.d: The mantissa bits plus the implicit bit: E4M3 has 4, BF16 has 8, FP16 has 11 and FP32 has 24. A product of p and q significant bits has at most p + q bits.

produto-exato.d: A product is exact in a format when it fits without rounding, that is, when p + q ≤ the target's significant bits and the exponent is within range. E4M3 × BF16 (4 + 8 = 12 ≤ 24) and BF16 × BF16 (16 ≤ 24) are exact in FP32.

upcast.d: Converting to a wider format (e.g., E4M3 → BF16/FP16/FP32). When the target has at least the source's significant bits and range, the upcast is exact: no value changes.

gib-gb.d: 1 GiB = 230 = 1,073,741,824 bytes; 1 GB = 109 bytes (7.4% less). vLLM and PyTorch count in GiB, while model cards and manufacturers usually count in GB: --kv-cache-memory-bytes 11811160064 is 11 GiB, or 11.81 GB.

contracao-fma.d: A compiler optimization that replaces a*b + c with a single FMA, with one rounding instead of two. The result changes in the last bits. In nvcc it is on by default and turned off with --fmad=false.

invariancia-de-lote.d: The property of a kernel or an engine in which the bits of a row's result don't depend on how many, or which, other rows came in the same call. It requires that the partition of the sums (tiles, split-K, reduction order) not change with the batch size.

escala-potencia-de-dois.d: A scale factor of the form 2<sup>k</sup>. Multiplying or dividing a float by it only changes the exponent field and rounds nothing, barring overflow or underflow. It's the idea behind E8M0/UE8M0 scales and TensorFold's FP8 KV.

ponto-fixo-numerico.d: A representation of fractions as integers with a fixed implicit scale: the integer q stands for q/2<sup>F</sup>. Integer sums are exact and associative, which is why TensorFold stores probability masses as 64-bit integers with F = 40.
